guide.file_invalid: The file {file} could not be read (invalid format).
guide.file_structure: The file {file} does not have the expected structure.
guide.name: The name
guide.no_help: No help text for this mode.
help.active.detail: Corresponds to the is_active field. When off, Clair is not active in this space and sending messages returns "no active agent". When on, it only acts if the rest of the settings are valid.
help.active.info: Turns Clair on or off in this learning space.
help.active.label: Clair active
help.avatar.detail: Choose one of the six illustrations. It is used in Clair's bubbles and in the message bar. This is a visual choice for this interface and is not sent to Clair. It takes effect immediately, with no need to save. The same avatar can be used by Clair and by a person (2 is the default for both).
help.avatar.info: Appears in the chat bubbles and bar. Only changes the look of this demo.
help.avatar.label: Clair's avatar
help.group.detail: Identifies the group that is talking. It is sent with every message and used in the periodic /pull check. The server keeps the dialogue state per group, and the “two people joined” greeting happens only once per group: reusing the same group continues the previous conversation. “New group” generates a new id (e.g., g-4f7a) and starts a clean conversation (the chat history is cleared too). Changing the group by hand also clears the chat. Groups on the blacklist (Blacklist tab) are blocked. Up to 50 characters. [to be confirmed]
help.group.info: Group of students talking in this space (up to 50 characters).
help.group.label: Group
help.kw.detail: They describe the topic of the students' activity. Clair compares the conversation with these keywords. Write one per line, up to 200 characters each. [to be confirmed by the author: how the comparison influences the intervention]
help.kw.info: Activity topics, one per line (up to 200 characters each).
help.kw.label: Keywords
help.lang.detail: Clair's language code, up to 5 characters (e.g., EN, NL). The list is the one the API returns for the chosen mode; if it fails to load, you can type the code. [to be confirmed by the author: effect of the language on Clair's utterances]
help.lang.info: Language code, up to 5 characters (e.g., EN, NL).
help.lang.label: Language
help.ls.detail: Name that identifies the learning space in Clair (up to 50 characters). These settings apply to this identifier, and chat messages are sent to it. Clair is only active if the settings are valid and "Clair active" is on.
help.ls.label: Learning space
help.mode.detail: The mode chooses the set of behaviors Clair uses in this space. The default is apt-base. The apt-goals mode can intervene without a triggering message; for this reason, this demo polls /pull periodically (see "Demo options"). Available languages depend on the mode. The "Which mode to choose?" guide just below summarizes the differences; it is a draft to be confirmed by the author.
help.mode.info: Sets Clair's operating mode. The default is apt-base.
help.mode.label: Mode
help.people.detail: Each name is sent to Clair as the message's user (username), up to 50 characters, and appears in the bubbles. Below each name, choose the person's avatar (six options); the avatar is visual only, is not sent to Clair, and appears in the speaker thumbnails and in the bubbles. Messages already sent keep the name and avatar they had when they were written.
help.people.info: Name and avatar of the 6 chat participants. Default: Person1 to Person6.
help.people.label: Participants
help.pull.detail: The interface polls the group's /pull endpoint every N seconds (minimum 5). This is what lets you see interventions without a triggering message, such as those of the apt-goals mode. Repeated interventions are discarded. The interval is the field next to it (minimum 5, default 30).
help.pull.info: Periodically checks whether Clair has something to say without being prompted.
help.pull.label: Proactive check (pull)
help.secs.label: Interval (s)
help.tech.detail: Shows, when present, intent, selected_move, dialogue_state and fuzzy_output, along with the raw JSON. Useful for researchers; off by default to keep the chat clean.
help.tech.info: Shows, under each message, the data Clair returned. Off by default.
help.tech.label: Show technical details in chat
hint.auth: Check CLAIR_TOKEN (Space Secret or .env file) and try again.

hint.no_cfg: There are no saved settings for this learning space. Click Save and activate.
hint.none_returned: The server returned no settings for this learning space. Click Save and activate.
hint.not_verified: Not verified yet. Click Save and activate.

hint.offline_ui: Could not reach Clair. Check that the service is running and CLAIR_URL, then try again.
hint.ready: Confirmed on the server at {time}: mode {mode}, language {cl_lang}.
hint.saved_unconfirmed: The settings were sent, but could not be confirmed on the server. {hint}

sim.lede: A group of simulated students (the **collabsim** package) chats in the learning space and group set in the Demo sub-tab. Each of their messages goes to Clair through the API, like a real student's, and Clair's interventions are relayed back to the students. While the simulation runs you only observe: the message box is hidden in the Chat.

sim.seed.info: Same seed and settings = same group (names, cards, misconceptions). Empty = random.
